Q: Need advice on how to represent solutions for the Bees Algorithm in maze pathfinding A:

you need to convert your maze to a weighted graph with a source and goal node, because that is what is used for A*. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_search_algorithm read this and make sure you understand how that representation works, because you need to imitate it. there's a picture on the page of A* being used to solve a random maze, so you could google how that's done, but i also see an obvious answer.

since your description involved four cardinal directions, you should consider the maze as a grid of nodes that are four-connected. so each has a connection to the east, north, south, west points around it. then for the walls of the maze, you'll just knock out certain connections. this would show how you couldn't travel east, for example, from a certain point in the maze. certain nodes could be entirely unreachable, and you can just wipe those from the graph. certain nodes could be entirely reachable. weights would show how long it takes to travel between different parts of the maze, if you need that. then you need your source and goal node - the start and exit of the maze.

if this is confusing, get out some graph paper and draw it. you'll be able to see why it works. once you have this, it's easy to generate endless random valid paths. i feel like the best path is always a tree so you should probably just generate those, but i don't know anything about BA, i'm just telling you about graphs here. so do what you think is best.

Q: Make overflow scroll bar visible on iOS and Android mobile A:

Apple made the conscious decision to HIDE scrollbars in iOS at the system level until there's an interaction. Mac OS (including Safari) and Android quickly followed that decision.

To the best of my knowledge, only the end user can override this setting and its system global.

The suggestion of finding a library to rebuild the scrollbars as discussed in How do I get scrollbars to show in Mobile Safari remains the best solution.

That said, I would have a VERY GOOD REASON before trying to force scrollbars on mobile devices. Users are trained not to need them and they take up pointless space on an already small screen.
